title: Lovable Review 2026: Features, Pros, and Cons
summary: Lovable turns a prompt into a React app with a Supabase backend and login wired in, and you keep the code. A research-based look at the credit model and the security work it leaves you.
body_markdown:
*Reviewed September 26, 2026. This is a research-based review of Lovable's official documentation, pricing and published customer feedback — not a hands-on benchmark. Jet Admin publishes this comparison and is a competing product; competitor strengths are stated as found.*


Lovable is worth considering when you want a working full-stack prototype from a description and intend to keep the code. Its strongest advantage is genuine code ownership through GitHub, which most AI builders do not offer. The trade-off is that credit consumption becomes hard to predict the moment a build gets complicated — and the security model stays your responsibility.


This review covers what Lovable produces, the features that matter for a business decision, the limitations to test before committing, what reviewers report, current pricing and how it compares with Jet Admin.


## Lovable review: the quick verdict


Lovable suits founders, designers and product people who need a real prototype fast and want a developer to be able to pick it up later. It is a weaker fit for applications with advanced permissions, approval chains or unusual data relationships — and for anything where you cannot own the security review.


Strong reasons to consider Lovable Trade-offs to evaluate


Prompt to a working React app with a Supabase backend, database and login Credit spend becomes unpredictable on complex builds


Clean code export via GitHub — you can continue in any editor Access control and row-level security are documented as your responsibility


Unlimited workspace members on every plan; priced by credits, not seats Reviewers report the AI struggling with auth logic and multi-step flows


Free plan with a daily credit grant, not a time-limited trial Credits expire, and the two mid tiers include the same allowance


No numerical score is given, because we did not run a scored hands-on evaluation.


## What is Lovable?


Lovable is an AI app builder: you describe an application in plain language and it generates a working React front end wired to a Supabase backend, with a database and authentication already connected. You then iterate in conversation.


The important distinction from tools that generate screens is that the output is a real, deployable codebase rather than a mockup — and you can take it. The important distinction from a managed platform is that Lovable does not absorb the operational responsibilities that come with owning a codebase.


Typical builds reviewers describe are landing pages, internal dashboards, MVPs and validation prototypes.


## Lovable's key features


### 1. Prompt-to-app generation with two build modes


Lovable distinguishes a default build mode from a planning mode. In default mode, work is metered by the change: documentation gives simple edits at 0.50 credits, removing a component at 0.90, adding authentication at 1.20 and a landing page with images at 1.70. Plan mode is a flat 1 credit per message.[Lovable pricing](https://lovable.dev/pricing)


That published table is genuinely useful, because it lets you estimate a build before paying for it. Note what it implies: the cost of a change scales with its scope, so an ambitious single prompt is not cheaper than several small ones.


### 2. A Supabase backend, database and authentication


New projects come with a backend, database and login already connected rather than assembled. For someone without backend help, this is what makes the output usable instead of decorative.


Scope this carefully before you rely on it. Supabase is a real database with real access-control semantics, and Lovable's documentation places row-level security and access control on you — a point the limitations section returns to.


### 3. Code ownership through GitHub


Lovable exports clean React code via GitHub integration, so development can continue in any editor. This is the feature that most distinguishes it in its category, and it changes the risk profile of starting here: a prototype that succeeds does not have to be rebuilt to be maintained.


If you are comparing AI builders, make this your first test. Generate something small, push it to GitHub, clone it and run it locally. The answer tells you more about your exit options than any feature list.


### 4. Seat-free collaboration


Workspaces support unlimited members on all plans, and Lovable states that plans "are priced by the credits they include, not by seats."


For a team where several people want to prompt, review and comment, that removes the usual per-editor arithmetic. The constraint moves entirely to credits, which is simpler to reason about but harder to forecast.


### 5. Cloud credits for AI features inside your app


Lovable distinguishes build credits, which you spend creating the app, from Cloud credits, which cover AI features running inside the app your users touch. The free plan includes monthly Cloud credits and a small allowance usable by AI features built into user apps.


This separation matters for budgeting: an app that calls AI at runtime has an ongoing cost that is independent of whether you are still building it.


## Lovable pros


### It is genuinely among the fastest routes to a working prototype


The most consistent finding across published reviews is that Lovable gets from a plain-language prompt to a functioning full-stack app faster than almost anything comparable, with the backend, database and login already wired. For validating an idea with real logins and real data, that is a material advantage.


### You keep the code, and that is rare here


Reviewers repeatedly single out code ownership as what sets Lovable apart from AI builders that lock you in. This is the strongest argument for choosing it over a platform whose backend you cannot take with you — and it is a legitimate reason to prefer Lovable even if another tool generates slightly better first drafts.


### Onboarding and interface quality are above the category norm


Clear navigation and guided setup come up often in reviews, with users reporting they built something real within hours. For non-technical builders, the difference between a tool you can navigate and one you cannot is the difference between shipping and abandoning.


### Credits, not seats, means the team can participate


Because pricing is credit-based with unlimited members, bringing in a colleague to review or prompt costs nothing extra. That is unusual and useful for small teams working on one app together.


## Lovable cons and limitations


### Credit spend becomes unpredictable past a simple build


The published per-change costs apply to clean, well-understood changes. Reviewers consistently report that spend turns unpredictable once a build gets complex, because the same feature may take several attempts.


**Who it affects:** anyone on Pro's 100 monthly credits attempting something intricate. **Scope:** customer reports, not a documented rate. **What to do:** during the free plan's daily grant, record credits per *completed and working* change rather than per prompt.


### Security and access control are left to you


This is the limitation most likely to matter to a business buyer. Lovable's own documentation places row-level security and access control on the builder, and a documented 2025 vulnerability exposed data across more than 170 Lovable-built apps before it was addressed.


**Who it affects:** any app holding data that is not public. **Scope:** the incident is historical and was addressed; the ongoing point is the division of responsibility, which is current and documented. **What to do:** if you cannot review Supabase row-level security policies yourself, budget for someone who can before the app holds real customer data. Generating an app is not the same as securing one.


### The AI struggles with the logic businesses actually need


Reviewers report the AI fumbling authentication logic and multi-step flows, and note that advanced permissions, billing rules, nested workflows, approvals or unusual data relationships require multiple iterations and manual cleanup.


**What to evaluate:** take your most awkward real rule — a two-stage approval, a role that can see some records but not others — and make that your first prompt, not your last. That single test predicts the rest of the project.


### Quality degrades on larger projects, and credits expire


Published reviews converge on Lovable being better for prototyping than long-term production applications, with debugging generated code described as frustrating at scale. Separately, credits expire: monthly credits after two months, annual credits a month after the annual period ends, and top-up credits after twelve.


**What to do:** do not buy credits ahead of a project that has not started, and treat Lovable's output as a strong first version that a developer will harden rather than a finished system.


## What do Lovable users say?


Published ratings on G2 and Product Hunt sit around 4.2 out of 5. We did not verify individual review counts for those figures, so treat them as indicative rather than precise.


**Positive themes:** speed from idea to working full-stack app; code ownership via GitHub; clear onboarding and interface; strong fit for landing pages, dashboards and MVPs.


**Negative themes:** unpredictable credit spend on complex work; AI errors in auth and multi-step logic; degraded quality and painful debugging on larger projects; the security model leaving meaningful work with the builder.


The themes are notably consistent in shape: reviewers like what Lovable produces first and distrust what it produces fifth. That pattern is the single most useful thing to take from the feedback.

Two things are worth noticing. Pro and Business include **the same 100 monthly credits** — the higher tier sells advanced controls and power features for growing departments, not more capacity. ## Jet Admin vs. Lovable: which should you evaluate?


The overlapping job is shipping a working business application without a development team. The approaches differ at the foundation: Lovable generates a new React app with a new Supabase backend, while Jet Admin builds an interface and workflows over a database or API you already have.


Priority What to evaluate


Your data already lives in Postgres, MySQL or an internal API Jet Admin connects to it. With Lovable, establish whether you are creating a second copy in a new Supabase project


You want to own and continue the code Lovable is the stronger choice — GitHub export is a real advantage and Jet Admin does not offer an equivalent codebase to take

### When Lovable is the better choice


If you need a standalone product with its own backend, and code you can hand to a developer, Lovable does something Jet Admin does not attempt. Its export story is a genuine strength and a legitimate reason to choose it.


## Who should use Lovable — and who should compare alternatives?


**Good fit:** validating a new product idea; a landing page or dashboard you want to own as code; a team without backend help that has someone who can review Supabase security; anyone whose plan is prototype now, harden later.


**Compare alternatives if:** the app must run on data you already own; your requirements centre on approvals, granular permissions or audit trails; you need SSO and documented governance for a security review; or nobody on the team can own row-level security.


If your case is an operational app on existing data with a lot of internal users,[build that on your own database with Jet Admin](https://www.jetadmin.io/) and compare it against a Lovable build of the same process.


## Lovable review FAQ


### What is Lovable?


An AI app builder that turns a plain-language prompt into a React application with a Supabase backend, database and authentication connected, with code you can export to GitHub.


### Is Lovable free?


There is a free plan with a daily grant of 5 build credits, up to 30 a month, plus 20 monthly Cloud credits. It is a permanent plan rather than a trial. Paid plans start at €25 per month including VAT as displayed in our region.


### Can I export my code from Lovable?


Yes — clean React code via GitHub integration, and you can continue development in any editor. This is the clearest advantage Lovable has over AI builders that retain your application.


### What does a Lovable credit cost me?


It depends on the change. Published default-mode examples are 0.50 credits for a simple edit, 0.90 to remove a component, 1.20 to add authentication and 1.70 for a landing page with images; plan mode is 1 credit per message. Retries consume credits too.


### Is Lovable secure enough for customer data?


Its documentation places row-level security and access control on you, and a 2025 vulnerability exposed data across more than 170 Lovable apps before being addressed. If you cannot review Supabase security policies yourself, get someone who can before holding real customer data.


### How does Lovable compare with Jet Admin?


Lovable generates a new app with a new backend and lets you keep the code. Jet Admin builds an interface over data you already have, with unlimited users and governance features on Business. Choose Lovable to own a codebase; choose Jet Admin when the data should stay where it is.


## Test the awkward rule first


Lovable's free daily grant is enough for the only experiment that matters: build the one screen with your hardest permission or approval rule, count the credits it takes to get right, and push the result to GitHub to confirm you can leave with it. Those two answers settle the decision.


If the exercise shows your data belongs where it already is,[try the same workflow in Jet Admin](https://www.jetadmin.io/) and compare what each approach asks you to take on.
